subject: Request: Dynamic Preemption Waiver for Reserved GPUs — Hydrangea Systems
messages:
From: Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@hydrangea-sys.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@hydrangea-sys.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Dynamic preemption waiver request for reserved GPUs

Hi Marissa / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We’ve been happy with Redwood’s Dedicated offering so far; the steady throughput and observability have been a big win for our inference pipeline. One thing we need to raise formally as we move towards contract execution: Hydrangea runs an overnight compliance batch between 01:00–03:00 PT that spikes ephemeral usage by ~2–3x for up to 20 minutes per night. Those windows must complete without preemption due to downstream reporting requirements.

From what I understand, reserved GPUs are subject to dynamic preemption during high cluster pressure. We’d like to request a temporary waiver (or a contractual carve-out) that pins our reserved nodes during our nightly batch window and for a short maintenance buffer afterwards. This would be a narrow SLA exception limited to our 01:00–03:20 PT window daily.

Attached is a night-of event sample (hydrangea-preempt-patterns.csv) showing the spike profile and the business impact notes. Can Redwood provide a proposed amendment (SLA addendum) that defines:
- the exact timebox for the waiver
- whether this is a hard pin vs. a higher-priority preemption threshold
- any cost/credit implications

We’re on a tight calendar — procurement needs the final language for signature by 2027-08-27 to meet our board compliance date. Happy to sync with product/legal as needed.

Best,
Aisha Varma
Head of Platform Reliability
Hydrangea Systems

Attachment: hydrangea-preempt-patterns.csv (text/csv)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@hydrangea-sys.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dynamic preemption waiver request for reserved GPUs

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear note and the sample. This is the right time to surface a narrowly-scoped exception like this rather than waiting for contract redlines. I’ve looped in Ben (account lead) and Stephanie (product SLA owner) so we can scope impact and draft an addendum.

Quick answers up front:
- We can evaluate a daily timebox carve-out pinned to your reserved pool but need to confirm feasibility across the cluster (we try to avoid hard pins because they reduce overall throughput efficiency).
- If a hard pin is required, it usually comes with an operational surcharge or a credit tradeoff; if we can implement a priority-bump (higher preemption threshold) instead, that may be lower cost.

Ben / Stephanie — can you review the attached usage profile and propose 1) a technical approach (pin vs priority-bump), 2) the SLA language draft, and 3) any estimated impact on our reserved pool utilization and cost? Aisha, I’ll aim to get a draft addendum back to you within two business days so procurement has time to review.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment referenced: hydrangea-preempt-patterns.csv (already attached)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example, Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@hydrangea-sys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dynamic preemption waiver request for reserved GPUs

Marissa / Ben / Aisha —

Thanks for the context and the CSV — looked through the spike samples. Technical summary and proposal below.

Technical notes:
- Your reserved pool is currently set with standard preemption tolerance (baseline fairness policy). A "hard pin" (no preemption) requires dedicated tenant isolation at the node level during the window — effectively preventing us from reclaiming capacity for transient demand.
- A lower-impact option is a "priority-bump": during the 01:00–03:20 PT window we raise your instance preemption threshold so only extreme cluster-wide pressure would evict you. This preserves cluster efficiency while giving you stronger tail guarantees.

Proposal (SLA addendum outline):
1) Timebox: Daily 01:00–03:20 PT
2) Mode: Priority-bump by two tiers (not an absolute hard pin)
3) Observable SLO: 99.95% successful completion of nightly jobs within the timebox over monthly windows
4) Mitigation & credits: If we miss the SLO more than twice in a rolling 30-day period due to preemption, Redwood will issue a monthly service credit equal to X% of reserved monthly fees (TBD in contract) and prioritize capacity remediation.
5) Exceptions: Force majeure, major datacenter outages; any hard pin requests would be priced separately.

I can draft the addendum text and attach a redline for procurement. Ben / Marissa — I’ll need an estimate for the commercial trade (credit vs surcharge) and whether Hydrangea would accept the priority-bump mode in principle.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Product Manager, SLA & Platform
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example

Attachment: sla-addendum-draft.pdf (draft outline)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Aisha Varma <aisha.varma@hydrangea-sys.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dynamic preemption waiver request for reserved GPUs

Aisha —

Appreciate the flexibility; Hydrangea’s use case (compliance batch) makes total sense. Commercial framing below:
- Priority-bump mode (Stephanie’s proposal) — no change to base monthly fee, but we include an SLO with credits. Estimated credit band: 5–8% of monthly reserved commitment per qualifying miss (exact percentage depends on pool size; I’ll get concrete numbers once Stephanie confirms expected residual capacity impact).
- Hard pin (no preemption) — available as a paid add-on. Estimated surcharge roughly 12–18% on top of reserved list price for full nightly pin (depends on region and node sizing).

Next steps: 1) Stephanie to send the redline addendum; 2) I’ll run commercial sims and return credit percentages by EOD Thursday; 3) Hydrangea procurement can review DocuSign once we align on the band.

If you’re OK in principle with the priority-bump + credit approach, we’ll fast-track a redline and send to DocuSign.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
ben_carter@redwood.example
+1 (650) 555-0147

Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dynamic preemption waiver request for reserved GPUs

Thanks — that commercial framing helps. Hydrangea prefers the priority-bump approach if the SLO/credit terms are acceptable. Procurement has requested the following clarifications before sign-off:
- The exact SLO definition and measurement window (monthly vs rolling 30-day) — we prefer rolling 30-day.
- Exact credit % per qualifying miss and a cap on aggregate credits per month.
- A short remediation SLA (e.g., Redwood commits to capacity remediation steps within 48 hours of two failures in 30 days).

We’ll mark procurement’s preferred language in the redline when you send the draft. If you can get the redline and an estimated credit table to us by EOD Monday (2027-08-23), we’ll aim to circulate for legal review and aim to sign by 2027-08-27 as requested.

Appreciate the responsiveness — this will make the deployment path much smoother.

Best regards,
Aisha
